reports.verdict: Shopify grew revenue 32% and lifted its cash margin to 22%, meeting its own forecast, with growth cooling from last quarter's 34%.

takeaways.label: Growth steady, not accelerating
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 32% to $3.74 billion, in line with the low-thirties forecast and down from 34% last quarter. Sales volume on the platform rose 29% to $119 billion. The Q4 forecast is again low-thirties.

takeaways.label: Profit growing much faster
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 66% to $568 million, and free cash flow margin reached 22% versus 18% a year ago. Losses from payments and loans fell to $120 million from $148 million.

takeaways.label: Gross profit lags revenue
takeaways.text: Gross profit grew 28%, slower than the 32% revenue growth, as lower-margin payments drove growth. Q4 gross profit is guided to the high-twenties.

takeaways.label: Large buyback begins
takeaways.text: Shopify spent $562 million repurchasing its own stock in the quarter, versus nothing a year ago. Cash and investments of about $4.7 billion remain.

reports.verdict: Chemicals growth and lower interest costs lifted profit, but the print business weakened sharply and now earns almost nothing.

takeaways.label: Print profit nearly gone
takeaways.text: Print revenue fell 7% to $165 million and its operating profit dropped from $8 million to $1 million, mainly on higher aluminum costs and lower volumes.

takeaways.label: Chemicals carry the company
takeaways.text: Advanced Materials & Chemicals revenue rose 21% to $99 million and profit rose to $21 million, but growth slowed from 40% last quarter.

takeaways.label: Profit helped by less debt
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $21 million from $13 million mainly because interest expense fell from $18 million to $3 million. Operating profit (EBITDA) edged up just $2 million to $31 million.

takeaways.label: Cash rebuilt
takeaways.text: Cash rose $27 million to $317 million after last quarter's inventory-driven drop. Operations were only break-even for the year so far, and stock compensation jumped.

reports.verdict: AMD's AI rack ramp is now showing up in sales, with Q4 revenue guided about $1B above estimates and 2027 growth raised above 80%.

takeaways.label: Q4 guide far above
takeaways.text: Fourth-quarter revenue is guided to about $17 billion, versus a $16.2 billion analyst average. Q3 revenue was $13.38 billion, up 45% and above the roughly $13.1 billion expected.

takeaways.label: 2027 growth raised
takeaways.text: CEO Lisa Su now expects total 2027 revenue to grow more than 80%, with server revenue doubling. AI chip growth is projected to be faster than previously forecast.

takeaways.label: Helios ramp begins
takeaways.text: Q3 was the first quarter of revenue from MI455 chips and Helios racks. Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Oracle are starting to use them, and shipments rise sharply in Q4.

takeaways.label: Margins flat, PCs weak
takeaways.text: Gross margin is guided to about 55%, slightly below the 55.3% expected. Gaming fell 40%, and Su expects the 2027 PC market to decline by double digits.

reports.verdict: Teva raised 2026 guidance again as Austedo, Ajovy and Uzedy grew fast, but total revenue still fell 2% on weaker generics.

takeaways.label: Guidance raised again
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue outlook rose to $16.7–17.0 billion from $16.5–16.85 billion. Austedo, Ajovy and Uzedy forecasts were all lifted. Profit guidance was left almost unchanged at $1.92–2.11 per share.

takeaways.label: Brand drugs drive growth
takeaways.text: Austedo sales were $751 million, up 21%. Ajovy reached $269 million, up 61%, and Uzedy $85 million, up 96%. Austedo's full-year target now sits at $2.55–2.65 billion.

takeaways.label: Margins widened
takeaways.text: Adjusted gross margin rose to 58.7% from 55.3%, and adjusted operating margin to 31.7% from 28.9%. Adjusted EPS was $0.86 versus $0.78 a year ago.

takeaways.label: Generics drag, deals weigh
takeaways.text: Revenue of $4.4 billion fell 2%, mainly on lower U.S. sales of generic lenalidomide. Reported EPS dropped to $0.20 from $0.37. New schizophrenia injection Weltruza is cleared for launch, and BXCL-501 is under FDA review.

reports.verdict: Pfizer raised its 2026 outlook, but a COVID collapse left quarterly sales flat, with the rest of the business growing 7%.

takeaways.label: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: Full-year revenue outlook rose $1.5B at the midpoint to $62-64B, and adjusted EPS to $2.95-3.05 from $2.80-3.00, even after a roughly $0.10 licensing charge.

takeaways.label: COVID drag, core growth
takeaways.text: Third-quarter revenue of $16.6B was flat. Paxlovid fell 63% and Comirnaty 29%, while sales excluding both grew 7% and newer or acquired products grew 32%.

takeaways.label: Eliquis boosted by pricing
takeaways.text: Eliquis rose 25% (+$513M), driven mainly by higher U.S. net price from lower rebates and favorable channel mix, so part of the growth may not recur.

takeaways.label: Vaccine and spending pressure
takeaways.text: Prevnar fell 10% on lower U.S. vaccination rates and lost adult market share. R&D spending rose 18%, so adjusted EPS stayed flat at $0.87.

reports.verdict: Refining profits hit another record on war-inflated margins, and management expects them to stay high through mid-2027 while it sells two refineries for cash.

takeaways.label: Record margins again
takeaways.text: Profit per barrel refined jumped to $45.70 from $17.60 a year ago. Adjusted earnings were $26.93 a share, above the roughly $24.5 analysts expected.

takeaways.label: Margins seen lasting
takeaways.text: Management expects elevated margins through at least mid-2027, citing about 10 million barrels a day of global refining capacity offline, and says it has seen no demand destruction.

takeaways.label: Selling two refineries
takeaways.text: Marathon is selling its St. Paul Park and Mandan refineries to CVR Energy for $4.2 billion, with $3.45 billion going to Marathon. Proceeds go mainly to the Gulf Coast.

takeaways.label: Heavy cash return
takeaways.text: Marathon returned $3.3 billion in the quarter, raised its dividend 10% and added a $5 billion buyback authorization. It holds $13.6 billion in cash.

reports.verdict: Record quarter, but Apple guided December gross margin down to 45%–46% as memory costs climb, and gave no outlook past that.

takeaways.label: Margins squeezed by memory
takeaways.text: December-quarter gross margin is guided to 45%–46%, below the 47.9% just reported (about 1 point of which came from tariff refunds) and below the 46.3% analysts expected. Memory prices are still rising.

takeaways.label: Growth slowing
takeaways.text: December-quarter revenue is guided up 7%–10%, down from 12% this quarter. Services is guided up 8%–9%. Mac and iPad supply stays limited by memory availability.

takeaways.label: AI spending climbing
takeaways.text: Operating expenses are expected to rise 11%–13% next quarter on AI investment. R&D already jumped about 32% to $11.7 billion in the September quarter.

takeaways.label: Strong quarter and year
takeaways.text: Revenue was $114.5 billion (up 12%) and EPS $2.10, both September-quarter records. iPhone grew 17% to $57.6 billion and Greater China grew 21%. Full-year revenue hit $479 billion.

reports.verdict: Palantir's growth is still accelerating: revenue nearly doubled, U.S. commercial passed U.S. government for the first time, and full-year guidance was raised again.

takeaways.label: Growth keeps accelerating
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 96% to $2.313B, the first quarter above $2B, with a 62% adjusted operating margin. Full-year revenue guidance rises to about $8.53B from about $8.15B.

takeaways.label: Commercial overtakes government
takeaways.text: U.S. commercial revenue hit $984M, up 148% year over year and 29% from last quarter, passing U.S. government revenue ($953M) for the first time.

takeaways.label: Cash machine
takeaways.text: Adjusted free cash flow was $1.216B, a 53% margin. The company holds $10.4B in cash and Treasuries. Full-year free cash flow guidance is $4.8–5.0B.

takeaways.label: New deals lag revenue
takeaways.text: New contracts signed (total contract value) rose only 6% to $2.92B, and U.S. commercial remaining deal value grew just 4% from last quarter. Revenue growth is far outpacing new bookings.
